_comment: The ISS daily exercise plan shown on the Exercises page. Machines, loads and the ~2 hours/day total come from NASA / CSA (links in 'sources'); per-exercise minutes are our split of that total for the demo. 'match' lists words in an NFC tag's label that count a tag workout toward that exercise.

exercises.name: Treadmill
exercises.summary: Running in microgravity, held onto the belt by a harness and bungee cords.
exercises.why: Every footstrike loads the hips, legs and spine, which slows the bone loss that weightlessness causes.

steps.title: Put on the harness
steps.text: Waist belt and shoulder straps, snug but comfortable.

steps.title: Clip in the bungees
steps.text: Attach the bungee cords to the harness. They pull you down onto the belt so you don't float away.

steps.title: Set your speed
steps.text: Start easy and build up. T2 goes up to 12 mph.

steps.title: Run tall
steps.text: Land under your hips, keep your core tight and arms relaxed.

exercises.name: Cycling
exercises.summary: The station's exercise bike, minus the seat: you clip in and strap down instead.
exercises.why: In 0 g the heart works less and can weaken. Steady cycling keeps the heart and lungs fit.

steps.title: Clip in your shoes
steps.text: Put on cycling shoes and click them into the pedals.

steps.title: Strap in
steps.text: There's no seat in microgravity: use the waist strap and hold the handles.

steps.title: Set the workload
steps.text: Pick the resistance on the display for today's session.

steps.title: Pedal smoothly
steps.text: Keep a steady rhythm and breathe evenly the whole time.

exercises.name: Resistance Training
exercises.summary: Squats, deadlifts and presses against vacuum cylinders that act like free weights.
exercises.why: Heavy loads tell bones and muscles they're still needed. ARED gives up to 600 lb (272 kg) of resistance.

steps.title: Set the load
steps.text: Turn the loading lever to today's weight (0 to 600 lb).

steps.title: Get under the bar
steps.text: Bar across your upper back, hands just outside the shoulders, feet hip-width.

steps.title: Squat down
steps.text: Push the hips back, chest up, knees tracking over the toes.

steps.title: Drive up
steps.text: Push through your heels back to standing. Breathe out on the way up.

exercises.name: Stretching & Mobility
exercises.summary: Gentle reaches, side bends and a forward fold, anchored by foot loops.
exercises.why: The spine lengthens in space and back pain is common. Stretching keeps joints and the spine moving well.

steps.title: Anchor your feet
steps.text: Slide your feet into the foot loops so you stay in place.

steps.title: Reach up
steps.text: Arms overhead, lengthen through the whole spine.

steps.title: Side bends
steps.text: Lean slowly to the left, then to the right. Hold each for a breath.

steps.title: Forward fold
steps.text: Hinge at the hips and reach down, knees soft. Roll up slowly.
